correctness.rationale: Exact interval endpoint ordering gives a prefix nonneighbor set for each appended vertex. The signed independent-set sum satisfies Z_i=Z_(i-1)+s_i Z_(k_i), and greedy choice keeps all intermediates in {-1,0,1}. Mod-two invariance forces the final output to be 0 when N is even or ±1 when odd; the character diagonalization proves exact invertibility and odd-case inverse norm. The octahedral spectrum follows from a product formula with multiplicities 27,27,9,1. Standalone checker passed 996 cases plus the full 64-character boundary; finite checks are corroborative, not an all-order proof.

The indexed interpolation matrix theorem cannot dominate the claim: matrix nonsingularity of restrictions is distinct from nonvanishing of the full Walsh transform of the support indicator.

originality.rationale: The nearest dated primary literature proves unsigned enumerative recurrences for path powers, whereas the new result establishes a vertex-signed Fourier parity sufficiency for every interval graph, a sharp odd-case inverse norm, an explicit greedy construction and a noninterval boundary. Indexed signed Fourier path and windmill results are restricted special cases; no inspected source mathematically implies the all-interval statement. Public-index-only related items and unindexed equivalences remain historical risks.

value.rationale: A sharp, representation-independent parity criterion for independent-set Fourier invertibility over the entire graph class of interval graphs is a natural complete classification, with a linear-time singularity witness and exact odd-case conditioning. It strictly generalizes fixed path-power questions and supplies a meaningful all-graph-class boundary via the canonical noninterval octahedral graph. The result has potential utility for signed interval scheduling and Boolean deconvolution, without claiming stronger unproved projection bounds.
